What is UHC?

On this page

World Mutation (Post-Gen) ​

Mirrors the FAWE QueueExtent + ChunkHolder runtime, but in plain Bukkit/Paper so we don't depend on FAWE.

Reference FAWE source: other repos/FastAsyncWorldEdit-main/

FAWE concept → AetherUHC implementation ​

FAWEAetherUHC
QueueHandler.blockingExecutorAsyncSquareFillEngine semaphore
getChunkAtAsync + ticketChunkRegionRunner warmup window + ChunkTicketScope plugin tickets
TPS budget in QueueHandler.run()MutationBudget MSPT defer
ParallelQueueExtent per-chunk flushChunkRegionRunner per-chunk processing

Post-gen architecture ​

The original Skripts (-bigcrack.sk, cu.sk, up.sk) just wrote blocks one at a time with set block to air — fine for small maps because they sync-loaded chunks on demand, but on a 1600-radius map that watchdogs the server.

We port that exact block-write logic, but route every write through ChunkRegionRunner:

  1. The runner holds an ordered list of chunk coords (everything the transform needs to touch).
  2. Each tick it pins the cursor chunk + a warmup window (N chunks ahead) via Paper plugin tickets and schedules async loads.
  3. It waits until the cursor chunk is a full LevelChunk (not a ProtoChunk).
  4. It hands the loaded Chunk to the transform's per-chunk callback, which uses Chunk#setBlockData directly.
  5. After the callback signals done, it releases the cursor ticket and advances.

This avoids three failure modes we hit before:

  • Sync load watchdog — world.getBlockAt(...).setType(...) on an unloaded chunk blocks the main thread; the runner only writes after async load completes.
  • Chunks unloading mid-write — without a plugin ticket, an async-loaded chunk can unload before the next tick; the runner pins until the chunk is fully processed.
  • FAWE no-op flush — the FAWE reflection bridge silently no-ops on flush() when the queue isn't owned by an EditSession, so tryFlushRegion advanced the progress bar without writing any blocks. Post-gen no longer touches the FAWE bridge at all — direct Chunk#setBlockData actually mutates the world.

Underground ParallelCell grid → X/Z column → Y source band → mirror to dest 54 belowCell-by-cell; per chunk in cell∩chunks: X/Z column → Y source → mirror writes (same chunk for source + dest)

Config (worldmanagement.yml) ​

WORLD-MUTATION:
  BLOCKS-PER-TICK: 12000          # cap blocks set per tick across all transforms
  MAX-MSPT: 50                    # defer when server tick exceeds this
  TICK-INTERVAL: 1                # ticks between scheduler runs (1 = every tick)
  DEFERRED-TICK-INTERVAL: 3       # slower interval when server is laggy
  ASYNC-CHUNK-WARMUP: true        # use Paper getChunkAtAsync (recommended; required for ticket flow)
  WARMUP-CHUNKS-AHEAD: 48         # chunk warmup window size (also caps tickets held at once)
  USE-FAWE: auto                  # FAWE bridge is initialized but post-gen no longer uses it
  CHUNK-APOCALYPSE-MAX-COLUMNS-PER-TICK: 4
  DRAGON-RUSH-SITES-PER-TICK: 2

Verifying the path ​

  1. Check the post-gen log line for the transform:
    • [Post-Gen] Big Crack carving N chunks (X chunks ..., Z chunks ...), 384 Y slices, budget 12000 blocks/tick.
    • [Post-Gen] Chunk Apocalypse: N cells (step 16, 5% delete), Y -64..319.
    • [Post-Gen] Underground Parallel: N cells (step 16), Mirror + bedrock seal.
  2. Watch the progress lines tick up by chunk/cell. If they stall on the same chunk for >30s, the cursor chunk isn't reaching LevelChunk status — check Paper's chunk system load.
  3. Visit the world; blocks should actually be air/mirrored.

Border defaults ​

The standard UHC start border is 2000 blocks (BORDER.START: 2000 in uhcconfiguration.yml). This value is divisible by 16, giving a clean 125-chunk radius (~63,001 chunks in the pregen square). All modern testing and post-gen uses BorderManager.getStartBorder() → BORDER.START as mapRadius.

Non-divisible-by-16 values (e.g. 1750) still work — the Underground Parallel transform now clamps partial edge cells instead of refusing to run — but 2000 avoids edge cases entirely.

UHC-WORLD-USED trigger ​

Pregen only runs when UHC-WORLD-USED: true in uhcconfiguration.yml. The flow:

  1. WorldsManager.startLoading() checks isMapUsed().
  2. If true → delete old world → recreate → scheduleWorldBorderFill(worldName, borderSize) → pregen starts.
  3. If false → load existing world, skip pregen.
  4. On pregen completion, onMapGenerationComplete() sets UHC-WORLD-USED: false and saves config.

Common mistake: copying an old config with UHC-WORLD-USED: false to a fresh server — pregen never runs because the plugin thinks the world is already usable. Always set true when deploying a fresh map.

Pregen Optimizations & Persistence (Paper 26.1+ / Legacy 1.8) ​

On modern and legacy versions, pregen speed and memory footprint are highly optimized through the following system:

  1. Environment Suppression: Before pregen starts, PregenEnvironmentManager suppresses non-essential server tasks: disables mob spawning, disables daylight/weather cycles, disables fire tick/random tick speed, and slashes the server's view-distance/simulation-distance to 2 to minimize loaded neighbor chunks.
  2. Memory-efficient Iteration: Pregen uses a simple row-scan iterator instead of a spiral iterator. This significantly increases generation throughput and simplifies the math.
  3. Chunk Batching & Periodic Saves: Previously, AsyncSquareFillEngine pinned all chunks for the entire duration of the pregen run. For large map sizes, this resulted in thousands of tickets held in memory, causing OOM crashes. The engine now batches chunk tickets (e.g., 2000 at a time) or saves based on a timer (SAVE-INTERVAL-SECONDS), flushes them to disk with world.save(), and releases the tickets.
  4. Urgent Priority: On Paper, world.getChunkAtAsyncUrgently is prioritized over the normal async chunk loading queue to squeeze maximum speed from the chunk generation threads.
  5. Disk Write Verification: The process finishes with a verification loop walking the expected coordinate grid to check world.isChunkGenerated() and logs any missing chunks.

Server-Level Tuning ​

For maximum throughput during pregen, ensure your server configurations have the following:

server.properties

  • sync-chunk-writes=false (CRITICAL for chunk gen speed)
  • view-distance=2
  • simulation-distance=2

Clean-slate test procedure ​

To validate pregen from scratch on a test server (e.g. test-server-26.1.2):

  1. Stop the server.
  2. Delete world data: world/ (including dimensions/minecraft/uhc_world*), plus any uhc_world folders.
  3. Reset plugin state: delete plugins/AetherUHC/uhcconfiguration.yml and worldmanagement.yml (or the entire plugins/AetherUHC/ folder).
  4. Set on the fresh config:
    • BORDER.START: 2000
    • UHC-WORLD-USED: true
    • CHUNK-PREGENERATION.PREGEN-MODE: async
  5. Deploy new plugin JAR(s), start server.

Expected log sequence:

Map pregen mode from worldmanagement.yml: async (world=uhc_world, halfSize=2000)
Map pregen (async): concurrent=320, startsPerTick=128
...
World map generation finished.
Map pregen: verified 63001/63001 chunks on disk (0 missing)

Disk check: world/dimensions/minecraft/uhc_world/region/ should have ~225 region files (chunk coords ±125 → region coords ±7, roughly 15×15).

Post-gen smoke test (in order): Big Crack → Chunk Apocalypse → Underground Parallel; confirm visible world changes and no hang on chunk 1.
